annotation.speech2: Level curves of h equals x squared minus y squared in the x y plane, with a legend to the right giving the value of c on each. Two black lines cross at the origin along the diagonals y equals x and y equals negative x. In the left and right regions between them are hyperbolas opening sideways, orange for c equals one and red for c equals two; in the top and bottom regions are hyperbolas opening up and down, light blue for c equals negative one and dark blue for c equals negative two.

The level curve where h equals zero is the pair of lines y equals x and y equals negative x, crossing at the origin. Every other level curve approaches these lines far from the origin: they are the asymptotes of all the hyperbolas.
The level curve where h equals one, the hyperbola x squared minus y squared equals one. It opens left and right, with vertices at plus and minus one on the x axis.
The level curve where h equals two, the hyperbola x squared minus y squared equals two, with vertices at plus and minus root two on the x axis, outside the curve for c equals one.
The level curve where h equals negative one, the hyperbola y squared minus x squared equals one. It opens up and down, with vertices at plus and minus one on the y axis.
The level curve where h equals negative two, the hyperbola y squared minus x squared equals two, with vertices at plus and minus root two on the y axis.
